title: VIP demands to skip the queue
symptom: A senior manager wants their small issue fixed before everyone else's
user_description: I'm the regional director. My second monitor is flickering and I need it fixed now, not after whoever else is in your queue.

options.text: Drop everyone else's urgent work and fix it immediately
options.why: Other tickets may affect whole teams. Priority should come from impact, not job title alone.

options.text: Tell him no and that he has to wait like everyone else
options.why: Being rude damages trust, and his issue may matter more than it seems.

options.text: Stay polite, check the real business impact, prioritise it if the company's policy or the impact justifies it, otherwise explain the queue honestly, give a time, and involve your lead if needed
options.why: This respects him and the other users. Many companies do have a VIP policy, so follow it, and let your lead decide on anything outside it.

options.text: Say yes, then work on it later anyway
options.why: A broken promise to a senior manager causes far more trouble than an honest answer.

hints: Does your company have a rule for senior staff?
Who can help if you are unsure?
real_world_tip: Ask what he needs the monitor for right now. A meeting in ten minutes is real business impact, and a quick swap may solve it.
